implementation_guide: Map this primitive to Azure AI Foundry Agent Service threads and messages. Keep one durable thread per active interaction, persist long-lived history outside the UI session, and summarize older turns before replaying them into the next model call.
best_for: Multi-turn copilots and durable agent sessions
limitations: Thread history alone is not a full memory strategy; long sessions still need summarization and external memory.
integration_notes: Pair Foundry threads with app-owned user/session IDs so telemetry and retention rules stay consistent.
evidence_note: Azure AI Foundry Agent Service exposes assistants or agents plus threads messages and runs as first-class resources.

guide_title: Prompt flow DAG or workflow graph
implementation_guide: Represent the step graph as a Prompt flow DAG: each node is a model tool or Python step, and edges move typed outputs downstream. Keep the graph acyclic so runs stay replayable and debuggable in the Foundry flow canvas.
best_for: Deterministic orchestration and debuggable multi-step flows
limitations: Open-ended multi-agent delegation fits Agent Service better than a rigid flow graph.
integration_notes: Use Prompt flow for bounded orchestration and let higher-level agent routing choose when to invoke the flow.
evidence_note: Azure AI Foundry Prompt flow uses node-and-edge flows for orchestration authoring execution and debugging.

implementation_guide: Treat each Prompt flow node definition as one node-list entry. Capture node name node type declared inputs or outputs and model or tool binding so the graph can be validated before deployment.
best_for: Flow validation release review and regression debugging
limitations: Node metadata drifts quickly if flow YAML and portal edits are not kept in sync.
integration_notes: Generate node inventories from the same source used to deploy the flow whenever possible.
evidence_note: Prompt flow authoring defines explicit nodes with typed inputs outputs and execution roles.

implementation_guide: Model the edge list from Prompt flow links between node outputs and downstream inputs. Keep data contracts explicit especially when chaining model outputs into tools so flow revisions do not silently break downstream steps.
best_for: Typed flow composition and lineage inspection
limitations: Weak schemas create brittle chains between model outputs and tool inputs.
integration_notes: Store input and output contracts near the edge mapping so reviews can catch schema drift early.
evidence_note: Prompt flow connections wire upstream outputs into downstream inputs and surface lineage during debugging.

implementation_guide: Use the Azure AI Foundry agent or assistant identifier as the stable agent_id. Keep it distinct from run IDs and thread IDs so telemetry permissions rollout state and cost records can all join back to one agent definition.
best_for: Agent cataloging telemetry joins and rollout management
limitations: Teams often confuse agent identity with run or thread identity.
integration_notes: Normalize Foundry IDs into one app-level registry before cross-service analytics.
evidence_note: Azure AI Foundry separates agent identity from thread and run resources.

implementation_guide: Derive capability tags from the tools knowledge sources and model settings attached to an AI Foundry agent. Tags should describe what the agent can do—not who owns it—using labels like file_search grounded_answering code_interpreter or web_lookup.
limitations: Capabilities inferred only from model names are too vague for robust routing.
integration_notes: Build tags from attached tools knowledge connectors and safety settings rather than hand-written blurbs.
evidence_note: Agent definitions in Azure AI Foundry bind tools and knowledge sources that determine effective capabilities.

implementation_guide: Normalize Azure lifecycle states into a small operational enum such as idle running awaiting_tool failed and completed. Do not overload status with business meaning; keep it operational so dashboards retries and escalation logic stay deterministic.
limitations: Raw provider states vary by surface and can leak too much detail into higher layers.
integration_notes: Keep one provider-to-platform status mapping table and reuse it across UI and automation.
evidence_note: Azure AI Foundry agent runs and tool calls expose execution lifecycle states that can be normalized for orchestration dashboards.

implementation_guide: Treat each applied Content Safety policy or moderation profile as a filter_id and version it per environment. This keeps moderation behavior traceable when the same app has different thresholds in dev test and production.
limitations: If moderation is configured ad hoc in code it becomes hard to explain production behavior later.
integration_notes: Version filter IDs per environment and log them with every moderation decision.
evidence_note: Azure AI Content Safety provides configurable safety policies and category thresholds that can be attached to AI application flows.

implementation_guide: Record the exact Azure AI Content Safety taxonomy or category version your app was validated against. When category definitions or severities change re-run evals before promoting the new taxonomy into production.
limitations: Taxonomy drift can invalidate prior moderation tuning without any code change.
integration_notes: Store taxonomy version in both config and evaluation artifacts.
evidence_note: Azure AI Content Safety classifies content by named harm categories and severity levels that evolve over time.

implementation_guide: Map Azure severity outputs to explicit actions—log flag redact or block—rather than treating every match as a hard stop. Keep that mapping beside the product config so reviewers can explain why a borderline case was allowed or blocked.
limitations: A single global action makes moderation either too noisy or too permissive.
integration_notes: Tie action policies to category and severity not just a binary safe or unsafe result.
evidence_note: Azure AI Content Safety returns category and severity signals that application logic can translate into policy actions.

implementation_guide: Tune thresholds per harm category instead of using one global cutoff. In AI Foundry blocking thresholds should be stricter than flag-only thresholds and any threshold change should trigger regression evals.
best_for: Threshold tuning and safety regression testing
limitations: One threshold for every category usually creates avoidable false positives or false negatives.
integration_notes: Track threshold changes like any other production config and re-run eval suites on every edit.
evidence_note: Azure AI Content Safety scoring is threshold-driven; applications decide when scores trigger enforcement.

implementation_guide: Use OpenTelemetry or Application Insights span IDs as the trace primitive for AI Foundry runs tool calls and downstream services. Every meaningful orchestration step should emit a span so one user request can be reconstructed end to end.
limitations: Without end-to-end spans Foundry run data and app telemetry stay fragmented.
integration_notes: Propagate trace context from user request to agent run to downstream tool call boundaries.
evidence_note: Azure Monitor and Application Insights use OpenTelemetry-style spans and trace IDs for distributed tracing.

implementation_guide: Set parent_span_id from the caller step that launched the next model or tool operation. This is what turns a flat run log into a debuggable trace tree for agent workflows.
limitations: Flat spans are easy to collect but poor for understanding orchestration structure.
integration_notes: Preserve parent-child relationships across async tool execution boundaries.
evidence_note: Distributed traces in Azure Monitor rely on parent and child span relationships to reconstruct causal trees.

implementation_guide: Name operations after the actual orchestration action—agent.run tool.search content_safety.check promptflow.node—not after internal class names. Good operation names make AI Foundry traces readable in dashboards and cost reviews.
limitations: Internal method names age poorly and hide business meaning.
integration_notes: Standardize operation names across agent service prompt flow moderation and retrieval steps.
evidence_note: Azure tracing and monitoring surfaces operation names as the primary grouping field for spans.

implementation_guide: Capture duration_ms on every model and tool span and compare it to a per-step latency budget. This is where you spot slow retrieval slow moderation or one runaway node inside an otherwise healthy AI Foundry run.
limitations: End-to-end latency alone does not reveal which step is actually slow.
integration_notes: Set explicit step-level latency budgets for model inference retrieval safety checks and tool execution.
evidence_note: Azure Monitor and Application Insights use duration as a first-class span metric for latency analysis.
